body.estimand_functional: Put \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\) and let \(b_n=n^{-2t/(4t+d)}\) for \(d\leq4t\), while \(b_n=n^{-4t/(4t+3d)}\) for \(d>4t\).  The proved all-regime statement is \(c n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\leq\rho_n^*\leq Cb_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  On the proved no-penalty subregion \(\alpha+\beta\geq\gamma\) and \(d\leq4\gamma\), \(\rho_n^*\asymp\rho_{n,e}^*\asymp n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\), with no logarithm at \(d=4\gamma\).  No independently derived repaired lower and upper maps have yet been proved equivalent.  The complete all-regime frontier, its unresolved transition logarithms, and the necessary direction of the known-propensity comparison therefore remain open; no common sharp-rate symbol is defined.

sampling_model.design: Project-specific strengthening: \(X\) is known to be exactly uniform on the entire cube \([0,1]^d\), not merely to have a bounded density or to be uniform on a support with holes.
sampling_model.units: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed observed margins of a law in \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary \(A\) has unknown propensity \(e\) under the observational experiment; the comparison experiment supplies the exact function \(e_P\) to the test.
sampling_model.outcome: Observed and potential outcomes are binary.  The pointwise boxes \(m_0,m_1\in[1/4,3/4]\) are project-specific fixed interior regression margins on the canonical continuous representatives.
sampling_model.overlap: The project-specific numerical overlap box is \(e(x)\in[1/4,3/4]\) for every \(x\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance estimator and no nuisance convergence rate is part of the class; all tuning is a deterministic function of \(n,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives a pointwise CATE-estimation minimax rate in a larger model with a merely bounded covariate density and real outcomes; Section 3.1 supplies localized fuzzy-hypothesis and Hellinger machinery.  Its binary lower submodel uses a density uniform on an \(n\)-dependent support-with-holes \(S_{h,k}\), so that lower bound does not transfer downward to the present exact full-cube uniform-design subclass.
Theorems 4 and 6 give fixed-alternative consistency and a local weak limit for quantitative homogeneity tests over structured rule classes under the paper's nuisance conditions.

Theorems 1--2 establish asymptotic normality for propensity-reweighted pairwise and multisample adjusted \(U\)-statistics under consistent propensity estimation, independent stratum samples, stable positive sample fractions, and pointwise overlap.

Section 3 derives joint asymptotic normality and Gaussian-simulation calibration for multisample \(U\)-statistics testing equality of additive treatment effects across a fixed collection of mutually independent prespecified strata.

Theorem 6 gives asymptotic level, fixed-alternative consistency, and nontrivial \(n^{-1/2}\)-local power for a multiplier-bootstrap test of homogeneous restricted CATE with possibly right-censored duration outcomes.

Section 4 gives a conservative finite-sample-valid Fisher randomization test for the sharp null of one unknown constant individual treatment effect by maximizing randomization \(p\)-values over a confidence set for that nuisance effect.

The main martingale-transformation results give asymptotic level for a permutation test of a constant marginal-distribution shift with an estimated nuisance shift, retaining exact level only for the more restrictive sharp null.
Theorems 3 and 7 give asymptotic chi-square tests of equality of finitely many score-defined group average treatment effects under complete randomization, with sample splitting or cross-fitting.

Theorems 4.1 and 5.2 give matching nonasymptotic binned conditional-independence radii for fixed discrete responses and a continuous conditioner under total-variation smoothness, a different null manifold and separation metric from constant CATE.

Theorems 6 and 7 give null validity and spline minimax power for projected conditional covariance under common smoothness and nondegeneracy restrictions, rather than a fixed-sample three-smoothness CATE radius.

Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 characterize bias, variance, and optimal separate wavelet resolutions for estimation of a signed expected conditional covariance functional; they guide nuisance resolution but do not test an unknown constant CATE.
The main minimax theorems derive sharp heteroskedasticity-detection rates using a squared first-difference proxy under a rough unknown mean.
Theorem 1 gives asymptotic normality and type-I error control for an intra-fold split CATE-variance statistic under explicit nuisance learner-rate conditions.
The paper proves that the propensity score is ancillary for semiparametrically efficient estimation of the regular average treatment effect under ignorability.
Theorems 3.3 and 3.4 give asymptotic null validity and consistency against smooth local sieve alternatives for the null that the conditional average treatment effect is constant.

The paper develops \(L_1\)-type tests based on uniformly consistent nonparametric kernel estimators for conditional treatment-effect restrictions and proves asymptotically correct size, fixed-alternative consistency, and power against some local alternatives.
Section 1 records the classical nonadaptive Hölder goodness-of-fit boundary, and the paper establishes the iterated-logarithmic price of adaptation in wavelet testing.

body.tldr: Let \(s_0=\alpha+\beta\).  The observational critical radius now has an original fixed-sample nuisance lower bound in the sparse collision regime: if \(d\geq2s_0\), then \(\rho_n^*\geq c\max\{n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)},n^{-2s_0/(2s_0+d)}\}\), with no logarithm at \(d=2s_0\).  The existing explicit profiled fourth-order test still gives the all-regime upper rate \(b_n\), and the no-penalty region \(s_0\geq\gamma\), \(d\leq4\gamma\) remains matched.  At \((d,\gamma,\alpha,\beta)=(1,1,1/10,1/10)\), the sharper bracket is \(c n^{-2/7}\leq\rho_n^*\leq Cn^{-4/19}\), while \(\rho_n^*/\rho_{n,e}^*\geq c n^{4/35}\).  The complete upper frontier remains open because the proposed pair-factor statistics are blind to a legal covariance-masking alternative; no common sharp-rate symbol is defined.

project_justification.gap: Published CATE-homogeneity procedures and adjacent minimax results do not give the fixed-sample critical radius on this project-specific binary exact-uniform class.  The new direct-Hellinger construction determines a nuisance-driven converse throughout \(d\geq2(\alpha+\beta)\), but the best available upper map does not match it outside the established no-penalty region, and the dense collision regime remains unresolved.
project_justification.niche: The live niche is the interaction among a composite unknown-constant CATE null, separately rough propensity and baseline functions, exact full-cube design, and connected repeated-cell collisions.  A sharp result must combine a componentwise homogeneous null prior with an omnibus signal richer than binned covariance factors and must control all sparse and dense occupancy projections.
project_justification.fill: The paper now supplies the explicit total profiled fourth-order test and all-regime upper bound, the known-propensity benchmark and matched no-penalty region, and a same-class fixed-\(n\) lower construction giving \(n^{-2(\alpha+\beta)/(2(\alpha+\beta)+d)}\) whenever \(d\geq2(\alpha+\beta)\).  At the canonical rough tuple this improves the converse to \(n^{-2/7}\) and proves a polynomial cost of unknown propensity.  The covariance-masking witness precisely explains why the attempted pair-factor upper statistic does not close the remaining frontier.

body.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 remains a method donor rather than the source of the present class: its pointwise-estimation model is larger and its binary lower submodel uses a support with holes.  The new converse uses the localized fuzzy-hypothesis idea only after proving exact full-cube uniform masses, componentwise binary margins, a common sign-conditioned singleton predictive law, and a bounded-overlap connected-graph Hellinger calculation on this class.  NeykovBalakrishnanWasserman2021 gives collision-sensitive conditional-independence testing under a different null and metric; LundborgKimShahSamworth2024, corresponding to PCM arXiv:2211.02039, gives projected-covariance validity and spline power under common-smoothness conditions; DukesStensrudBrioschiHudson2026, arXiv:2410.00985v4, gives asymptotic structured-rule homogeneity results under nuisance conditions; and McGrathMukherjee2026, arXiv:2212.14857v5, derives separate resolutions for estimating a signed expected conditional covariance.  None supplies the componentwise constant-null, original fixed-sample nuisance lower map proved here, nor an omnibus test that overcomes the displayed covariance-masking alternative on the identical class.
body.technical_internal_limitation: With \(s_0=\alpha+\beta\), the optimized lower construction takes \(h\asymp\delta^{1/s_0}\), \(H\asymp\max\{h,\delta^{1/\gamma}\}\), \(q_e=2\delta^{\alpha/s_0}\), and \(q_b=2\delta^{\beta/s_0}\).  Original margins bound every conditional binary cell probability below by \(1/16\).  Conditional on macro signs, exact singleton matching and fine-coordinate independence give a connected-component discrepancy bounded by \(C^k\delta\); exact uniform design and a spanning-tree count then give \(H^2\leq Cn^2h^d\delta^2\sum_{k\geq2}(Cnh^d)^{k-2}\).  This yields the stated rate when \(d\geq2s_0\), including the equality boundary after choosing a small fixed amplitude.  When \(d<2s_0\), \(nh^d\to\infty\) at that scale and this summation does not control high-order connected clusters.  The fixed-reference fifth projection remains a valid warning about that normalization, but it is absent after common-singleton normalization.  The upper-side obstruction is different: a legal alternative annihilates every proposed population kernel with the specified within-bin pair factor, so a full-cell alternative dichotomy and its concentration theory are still required.
body.honest_scope: The causal estimand and statistical class remain unchanged: binary outcomes, exact uniform design on the full cube, fixed overlap and interior margins, three fixed Hölder indices, and an unknown constant null.  No nuisance-rate, learner, or estimator-side condition was added.  The proved content is an all-regime bracket, a matched sufficient no-penalty region, and the new sparse-regime nuisance converse; at the rough stress tuple the remaining exponents are \(2/7\) and \(4/19\), so the frontier is not claimed sharp.  The strict known-versus-unknown region certified by the new lower bound is sufficient, not necessary.  Dense-regime lower optimization, the omnibus upper construction, and unproved transition logarithms remain open.  No result certifies an existing causal forest, and non-rejection is not evidence of homogeneity.
body.interpretation: In sparse rough-nuisance regimes, repeated-cell scarcity creates a detectability cost that persists without positing any nuisance estimator.  At \((1,1,1/10,1/10)\), heterogeneity smaller than order \(n^{-2/7}\) cannot be uniformly detected when the propensity is unknown, whereas supplying it permits order \(n^{-2/5}\); the radius ratio therefore grows at least as \(n^{4/35}\).  This is a worst-case experiment comparison and a benchmark for workflow design, not a validation of a fitted forest or a license to interpret non-rejection as constant treatment effect.
